clue.text: Lorry drivers cut risk drastically, bypassing centre of Leeds

indicators.note: the scrambled letters pass around the single Leeds letter, so it sits within them
cut and risk treated drastically are thoroughly rearranged
the centre of the five-letter word Leeds is its middle letter

explanation.surface: Haulage drivers take a big gamble by avoiding the middle of a Yorkshire city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drastically' makes TRUCKIS, which 'bypassing' wraps round the middle of Leeds. A truckie is Australian slang for a lorry (truck) driver.
explanation.definitionFit: Truckie is informal, chiefly Australian, slang for someone who drives a truck for a living.

clue.text: Soldiers entering ruins of Thrace to join up again

indicators.note: the soldiers go into the jumbled letters, so one piece is placed inside the other
the ruins of the word Thrace are its letters knocked into a new order

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops march into a ruined ancient region in order to reunite it.
explanation.definitionFit: To reattach something is to fasten it back on, connecting the pieces once more.

clue.text: I'm able to support actor from part of south America

indicators.note: in a down entry a supporting piece sits beneath the other, so it comes second

parts.note: a co-star is an actor sharing top billing
I can means I'm able, said of oneself

explanation.surface: Someone offers to back up a performer who comes from a Latin American country.
explanation.definitionFit: Costa Rica is a nation of Central America, which the clue loosely counts as a southern part of the Americas; the adjective names one of its people.

clue.text: One music fan enters seedy bar, at first in a mood

indicators.note: at first places the word in at the very front of the build
one piece enters the other, so it goes inside the bar's letters

parts.note: a dive is a seedy, disreputable bar
the Roman numeral for one
cat is old jazz slang for a music fan

explanation.surface: A lone jazz lover walks into a grotty bar, feeling moody at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a mood' looks like a feeling, but the mood is the grammatical kind; 'enters' and 'at first' place the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar the indicative is the verb mood used for plain statements of fact, as opposed to the subjunctive or imperative.

clue.text: Like the writing in Charlotte's web?

definitions.text: Like the writing in Charlotte's web?

parts.words: Like the writing in Charlotte's web?
parts.note: in the children's novel Charlotte's Web the spider Charlotte weaves words into her web, so that writing is thin, scrawly and made by an arachnid

explanation.surface: A question about the messages spun in a famous children's book.
explanation.definitionFit: Spidery handwriting is thin and straggly, and Charlotte's written words were literally made by a spider.

clue.text: Notes found in settee

parts.note: so (soh) is a note of the sol-fa scale
fa is another note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Musical notes turn up down the back of the couch.
explanation.definitionFit: A settee and a sofa are the same upholstered seat for two or more people.

clue.text: Liquor store fixed up time and date of first delivery?

indicators.note: in a down entry, fixed up has the whole build reading upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: an age is a long period of time
DOB, date of birth, is the date one was first delivered into the world

explanation.surface: A wine shop arranges the timing of its first consignment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'date of first delivery' is a playful description of a birthday, giving DOB. BODEGA is Spanish for a wine shop or cellar.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodega is a Spanish wine cellar or shop selling alcohol, so a store for drink.

clue.text: Supplier of rings for the jeweller's, perhaps

definitions.text: Supplier of rings for the jeweller's, perhaps

parts.words: Supplier of rings for the jeweller's, perhaps
parts.note: rings here are chimes, not jewellery: a jeweller's premises, like any store, may have a device that rings when the door opens

explanation.surface: A firm providing wedding bands to a jewellery shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorway bell in a store rings to announce each customer, so it supplies rings.

clue.text: Dismiss bands making comeback

indicators.note: making a comeback, the bands' letters return the way they came, read backwards

parts.note: a hoop is a circular band
a second hoop, the plural bands giving two of them

explanation.surface: Someone waves aside groups staging a reunion tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bands' looks like pop groups but means hoops; two of them reversed by 'making comeback' give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To pooh-pooh an idea is to dismiss it scornfully as unworthy of attention.

clue.text: Got a good grade, presumably, in oral history

indicators.note: oral means spoken, so the word for history is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: the past is history, what has gone before

explanation.surface: A student did well, presumably, in a spoken history exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oral history' reads as an exam subject, but 'oral' turns PAST into a word that sounds the same. 'presumably' is there because a pass need not be a good grade.
explanation.definitionFit: A student who passed an exam met the required standard, presumably earning a decent mark.

clue.text: Mischief maker holding in hand dodgy drug is a cannabis supplier

indicators.note: the mischief maker holds the rest of the letters, so they sit inside it

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous little sprite

indicators.note: dodgy suggests something not right, so in and hand are rearranged

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A troublemaker caught with a dubious substance turns out to be a pot dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' makes NDIANH, and 'holding' puts that, with the drug after it, inside the mischief maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Indian hemp is the plant Cannabis indica, the source of hashish and marijuana.

clue.text: Announced food and entertainment

indicators.note: announced means spoken aloud, so the word for food is heard, not spelt

parts.note: fare is food, as on a menu

explanation.surface: A notice proclaiming refreshments and a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A funfair offers rides and amusements, a form of entertainment.

clue.text: Breather needed in long-haul flight, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a breather here is anything one breathes through, such as the windpipe or a nostril
a long-haul flight is one example of a journey by air

explanation.surface: A passenger needs a rest during a very long flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breather' looks like a pause for rest; it is an airway in the body.
explanation.definitionFit: An air passage is both a respiratory tube in the body and a journey made by aeroplane.

clue.text: Opposition article is written about taxes

indicators.note: the article and is are written about, that is around, the taxes

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
tithes were taxes of a tenth paid to the church

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece on taxation draws opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written about' looks like the topic of a newspaper piece, but it is the container signal: the article and 'is' go round the taxes.
explanation.definitionFit: Antithesis is direct contrast or opposition between two things or ideas.

clue.text: Film strip we hear

parts.note: the band along a cinema film that carries the audio is the strip whose content audiences hear

explanation.surface: A piece of celluloid film that is listened to.
explanation.definitionFit: A soundtrack is the narrow band on movie film carrying recorded audio, and hence the music heard with it.

clue.text: Could be Prague hotel's noisy registration desk

indicators.note: noisy says the phrase for a Prague hotel is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: a hotel in Prague is a Czech inn

explanation.surface: A loud reception counter at a hotel in the Czech capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noisy' looks like a complaint about the hotel, but it signals that CZECH INN is spoken aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: The check-in is the counter where arriving guests or passengers register.

clue.text: City women in fashion put cloak on

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting the cloak on means it is placed above the rest

parts.note: a cape is a sleeveless cloak

indicators.note: the women's letter goes in the word for fashion

parts.note: ton is fashion, the fashionable world

explanation.surface: Fashionable women put on capes in a South African city.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Town is the legislative capital of South Africa, a major port city.

clue.text: Guest rudely hogs this dessert

indicators.note: the words Guest rudely hog, that is hold onto, the answer within them

explanation.surface: An ill-mannered visitor greedily keeps the pastry to themself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hogs' looks like greed but means the two words contain the answer. 'this' is a link pointing to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Strudel is a pastry dessert of thin layered dough rolled round a filling such as apple.

clue.text: Demand made in divorce court case?

parts.note: ex is the prefix for a former partner, someone after a divorce
an action is a lawsuit, a court case

explanation.surface: Claims made in a lawsuit over a marriage breakup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divorce court case' reads as one phrase but splits into two pieces; 'made in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An exaction is a demand for payment, especially a harsh or excessive one.

clue.text: Compliment that gets right up the wine taster's nose

definitions.text: that gets right up the wine taster's nose
definitions.meaning: the smell of a wine is what a taster draws up into their nose

explanation.surface: Praise that rather irritates someone sampling wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets right up the nose' looks like the idiom for annoying someone, but here it is a literal smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A bouquet is both a tribute or compliment and the aroma of a wine.

clue.text: Repaired brickwork: grouted central parts, as specified

parts.note: pointing is repairing the mortar joints in brickwork, so pointed means having done that

indicators.note: the central parts of grouted are its middle three letters

explanation.surface: Instructions for a builder on repairing and grouting a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central parts' takes the middle three letters of GROUTED, OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To point something out is to indicate it or draw attention to it, as when specifying.

clue.text: Do this as a rule when starting to write speech

definitions.text: Do this as a rule when starting to write speech

parts.words: Do this as a rule when starting to write speech
parts.note: as a convention, a new line of dialogue in prose begins set in from the margin

explanation.surface: Advice on the usual practice for setting out written dialogue.
explanation.definitionFit: To set the first line of a paragraph in from the margin is the usual way to begin each quoted remark.

clue.text: Attraction of the lottery?

parts.note: the appeal of a lottery is the weekly picking of numbers, and also anything that pulls people in

explanation.surface: Asking what makes a lottery appealing.
explanation.definitionFit: A draw is both an attraction that pulls in crowds and the random selection of lottery numbers.

clue.text: Awfully rude quotes concerning a style of architecture

indicators.note: awfully suggests a terrible mess, so rude and quotes are rearranged

explanation.surface: Offensive remarks are made about a building style.
explanation.definitionFit: Tudoresque describes building in imitation of sixteenth-century English Tudor design, black timbers and white plaster.

clue.text: Built-up town in Holland

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word for built reads from bottom to top

parts.note: made means built or constructed

explanation.surface: A developed, built-up Dutch town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Built-up' reads as one urban term, but it splits into MADE and a reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a Dutch town north of Amsterdam, famous for its round cheese.

clue.text: Sports venues don't get any cheaper, it may be said

indicators.note: it may be said means the phrase is spoken, so its sound gives the answer

parts.note: to stay dearer is not to get any cheaper

explanation.surface: Complaining that tickets at sports arenas never fall in price.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent STAY DEARER sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stadia is a plural of stadium, an arena for sport.

clue.text: Its content may be a lot more dry than is required

definitions.text: Its content may be a lot more dry than is required

parts.words: Its content may be a lot more dry than is required
parts.note: the European Union's surplus of unsold table wine, much of it dry, was stored in excess of demand

explanation.surface: Describing a document or body of text that is very dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dry' looks like dull or arid, but describes wine; the surplus is far more than anyone needs.
explanation.definitionFit: The EU's excess stock of wine was nicknamed a lake, like its butter mountain.

clue.text: Had time to go round outskirts of Swedish capital

indicators.note: the words for had and time go round the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: taken can mean had, as in had or taken a holiday

indicators.note: the outskirts of Swedish are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone had time to tour the suburbs of Stockholm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swedish capital' reads as Stockholm, but 'capital' alone is the definition; 'to go round' puts the outskirts inside the synonym for had, after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tashkent is the capital city of Uzbekistan.
